brief.scope:
Security audit of lane/session-20260916-g at aea65bb9 against origin/dev,
for #247. Three components; full detail and suite/probe readings taken at
this head are in in/scope-detail.md, read it whole before working:
1) W5, the Dispatcher role (boundaries.json row, matrix.py gate, the
   dispatcher.py lever, the state-engine machine, the holder_note seam).
2) testkit's host_path kwarg (LD-72).
3) W3's void rule now judging only the branch's own first-parent commits,
   never a trunk merge.
Audit only; do not edit the snapshot.

findings.claim: The Dispatcher gate is bypassed when dispatch.sh is invoked through bash or source; these forms execute the tracked dispatcher but are never classified as kind=dispatcher.
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
import sys
sys.path.insert(0,'ops/devlane/hooks/claude')
import matrix
for c in ('bash ops/bin/dispatch.sh --job plan','source ops/bin/dispatch.sh --job plan'):
 print(c, matrix.check_text(c,'.'))
PY

findings.claim: Handover authorization checks the agent identity, not holder_note's session. Two sessions using the same model identity can therefore seize the role before its TTL lapses.
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
import os,subprocess,sys,tempfile
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
 e=dict(os.environ,XDG_STATE_HOME=d,WF_AGENT_OVERRIDE='Shared Agent <shared@example.invalid>')
 for sid in ('session-a','session-b'):
  p=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'ops/conductor/tools/dispatcher.py','set','--why',sid],env=dict(e,CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=sid),text=True,capture_output=True)
  print(sid,p.returncode,p.stdout.strip())
PY

findings.claim: ambient_tools accepts traversal names. Resolution occurs relative to the caller, while wrapper placement occurs relative to world.bin, allowing creation of an executable outside the World that survives World.close().
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
import os,tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from ops.testkit import World
old=os.getcwd(); oldtmp=tempfile.tempdir
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
 d=Path(d); (d/'worlds').mkdir(); (d/'a/b').mkdir(parents=True)
 real=d/'escaped'; real.write_text('#!/bin/sh\n'); real.chmod(0o755)
 os.chdir(d/'a/b'); tempfile.tempdir=str(d/'worlds')
 try:
  w=World(host_path=False,ambient_tools=('../../escaped',))
  placed=(w.bin/'../../escaped').resolve(); print(placed,placed.is_relative_to(w.root.resolve()))
  w.close(); print('survives',placed.exists())
 finally:
  os.chdir(old); tempfile.tempdir=oldtmp
PY

findings.claim: Audited SHA fields are not validated as commit IDs or separated from git options. A record value beginning --output= is interpreted by git log, writes outside the repository, yields empty stdout, and makes the audit appear unvoided.
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
import subprocess,sys,tempfile
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0,'ops/devlane/hooks/claude'); import matrix
head=subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'],text=True).strip()
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
 print(matrix.branch_commits('.',f'--output={d}/escaped',head,''))
 print([str(p) for p in Path(d).iterdir()])
PY

findings.claim: --first-parent combined with --no-merges ignores every non-trunk merge as well as trunk-forward merges. A topic/session branch can therefore merge unaudited code and retain the old audit.
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
import subprocess,sys,tempfile
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0,'ops/devlane/hooks/claude'); import matrix
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
 r=Path(d)
 def g(*a): return subprocess.check_output(['git','-C',d,*a],text=True).strip()
 g('init','-q','-b','lane'); g('config','user.name','T'); g('config','user.email','t@example.invalid')
 (r/'x').write_text('x'); g('add','x'); g('commit','-q','-m','audit'); audited=g('rev-parse','HEAD')
 g('checkout','-q','-b','topic'); (r/'unaudited.py').write_text('x'); g('add','-A'); g('commit','-q','-m','code')
 g('checkout','-q','lane'); g('merge','-q','--no-ff','topic','-m','merge topic'); head=g('rev-parse','HEAD')
 g('update-ref','refs/remotes/origin/dev',audited)
 print(g('diff','--name-only',audited,head)); print('voided_by=',repr(matrix.voided_by(d,audited,head,'RID',0,('.dev/records/',),'dev')))
PY

findings.claim: The broad .dev/records/ exemption also exempts later edits to the audit record itself. Closed audit evidence can be rewritten after landing without voiding the audit, contrary to CONTRIB.md's stated rule.
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
import subprocess,sys,tempfile
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0,'ops/devlane/hooks/claude'); import matrix
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
 r=Path(d)
 def g(*a): return subprocess.check_output(['git','-C',d,*a],text=True).strip()
 g('init','-q','-b','lane'); g('config','user.name','T'); g('config','user.email','t@example.invalid')
 (r/'x').write_text('x'); g('add','x'); g('commit','-q','-m','audit'); audited=g('rev-parse','HEAD'); g('update-ref','refs/remotes/origin/dev',audited)
 p=r/'.dev/records/dispatches/RID.json'; p.parent.mkdir(parents=True); p.write_text('{"findings":[1]}'); g('add','-A'); g('commit','-q','-m','land record')
 p.write_text('{"findings":[]}'); g('add','-A'); g('commit','-q','-m','rewrite record'); head=g('rev-parse','HEAD')
 print('voided_by=',repr(matrix.voided_by(d,audited,head,'RID',1,('.dev/records/',),'dev')))
PY

findings.claim: Record validation treats one present member of each required pair as agreement and defaults an absent findings array to empty. A partial closed record missing model.ran, result.head, and its envelope is accepted.
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
import subprocess,sys
sys.path.insert(0,'ops/devlane/hooks/claude'); import matrix
h=subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'],text=True).strip()
r={'job':'security-audit','status':'closed','harness':{'name':'codex'},'model':{'requested':'wanted'},'snapshot':{'ref_sha':h}}
print(matrix.audit_of('.',h,'RID',r,{'MODEL_CODEX_SECURITY_AUDIT':'wanted','TRUNK_BRANCH':'dev'},('.dev/records/',)))
PY

findings.claim: A post-audit commit is exempted solely by Finding: and Verified: text. No relationship between the cited finding and changed paths is checked, so unrelated unaudited code can ride in a nominal fix commit.
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
import sys
sys.path.insert(0,'ops/devlane/hooks/claude'); import matrix
print(matrix.is_a_fix_for('unrelated code\n\nFinding: RID#1\nVerified: true','RID',1))
PY

findings.claim: The sandbox flag is fail-open for non-boolean values: bool('false') is True, silently appending the host PATH when the caller expressed a false value.
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
from ops.testkit import World
w=World(host_path='false'); print(w.host_path,w.env()['PATH'] != str(w.bin)); w.close()
PY

findings.claim: The holder_note seam validates only non-emptiness. Arbitrary multiline or credential text is persisted and echoed by set/show, violating the claim that the column contains only a session ID and enabling log/output injection.
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
import os,subprocess,sys,tempfile
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
 e=dict(os.environ,XDG_STATE_HOME=d,WF_AGENT_OVERRIDE='Agent <a@example.invalid>',CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID='real-session')
 subprocess.run([sys.executable,'ops/conductor/tools/dispatcher.py','set','not-a-session\ncredential=TOP-SECRET','--why','demo'],env=e,check=True,capture_output=True)
 print(subprocess.check_output([sys.executable,'ops/conductor/tools/dispatcher.py','show'],env=e,text=True))
PY
